1.w: The words of Agur son of Jakeh—the burden. An utterance of the strong man to Ithiel; to Ithiel and Ucal.

2.w: “Surely I [am] more brutish than man, and the understanding of man [is] not unto me.

3.w: And I have not learned wisdom or known the knowledge of holy ones.

4.w: Who has gone up [to] the heavens and descended? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has bound the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What [is] His name, and what [is] the name of His Son? Surely you must know!

5.w: Every word of God is refined; He [is] a shield for those taking refuge in Him.

6.w: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you, and you be found a liar.

7.w: Two [things] I have asked of You—do not withhold [them] from me before I die:

8.w: Put vanity and the word of a lie far away from me; do not give poverty or wealth to me; provide me the bread of my portion,

9.w: lest I become satisfied and I deny and say, ‘Who [is] YHWH?’ And lest I become dispossessed and steal, and I seize the name of my God.

10.w: Do not slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you and you be found guilty.

11.w: A generation lightly esteems its father, and does not bless its mother.

12.w: A generation [is] pure in its own eyes and yet has not been washed from its filth.

13.w: A generation—how high its eyes, and its eyelids are lifted up!

14.w: A generation—its teeth [are] swords and its fangs [are] knives, to devour the poor from the earth, and needy ones from mankind.

15.w: Unto the leech [are] two daughters—‘Give, [and] Give. Three [things] are never satisfied, four never say, ‘Enough!’:

16.w: Sheol, and the barren womb, earth not satisfied with water, and the fire never having said, ‘Enough!’

17.w: The eye [that] mocks at a father and despises obedience to a mother—the ravens of the valley will dig it out, and the young eagles will eat it.

18.w: Three [things], they are wonderful for me, and four, I cannot know them:

19.w: The way of an eagle in the heavens, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship in the midst of the sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.

20.w: This [is] the way of a woman committing adultery: She eats and has wiped her mouth and has said, ‘I have not done wickedness.’

21.w: For three things the earth has trembled, and for four it is not able to bear up:

22.w: Under a servant when he becomes king, and a fool when he is filled with food,

23.w: under a hated woman when she is married, and a maidservant when she dispossesses her mistress.

24.w: Four [things], they [are] small on the earth; they are wiser than wise:

25.w: The ants [are] a people not strong, and they prepare their food in the summer;

26.w: the rock badgers [are] a people not strong, and they set their home in the cliffs;

27.w: a king [is] not unto the locust, and go they forth in formation, all of them;

28.w: the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, and it [is] in the palaces of king.

29.w: Three [things], they [are] are doing well of step, even four are doing well in the walk:

30.w: A lion, mighty among the beasts, and it does not turn back from the face of anything;

31.w: one girded of loins, or a he-goat, and a king with his army around him.

32.w: If you have been foolish in lifting up yourself, and if you have schemed—hand to mouth!

33.w: For [as] the churning of milk brings forth butter, and pressing of the nose brings forth blood, so the pressing of anger brings forth strife.”
